meta.title: 3D bioprinted human iPSC-derived neural progenitor cells as a novel platform for studying neurogenic niche.

extracted_by: seed: Claude (Claude Code session), pending human review
summary: A Geltrex/GelMA blend was used to bioprint human iPSC-derived neural progenitors, which self-organized into neurogenic-niche-like clusters. Constructs stayed viable for over 110 days.

formulations.stiffness_note: storage modulus G' ~100 Pa at 1 Hz
formulations.review_notes: Viability shown qualitatively; no percentage in the text. Print method inferred from the methods description.
formulations.name: Geltrex / GelMA blend
formulations.composition_detail: 8% (w/v) GelMA with Irgacure (0.25% final) blended with Geltrex
formulations.key_outcome: Printed hNPCs self-organized into neurogenic-niche-like clusters and stayed viable for more than 110 days.

evidence.quote: An 8% (w/v) GelMA solution was prepared in PBS, and 0.5% (w/v) of the photoinitiator Irgacure was added
The bioink was extruded from a 5 ml syringe at an average printing speed of 3.3 mm/s, using a 22 G needle
oscillatory tests indicated that our hydrogel exhibited storage modulus values within this range as a 3D model (∼100 Pa)
